info.title: Touchmark API
info.description:
Validate email addresses: syntax, DNS/MX, disposable and free-provider domains, role
accounts and typo suggestions. Verify that a mailbox exists by asking its mail server.
Check a sending domain's DNS against the Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft bulk-sender rules.
Look up an IP address: country, network owner, hosting or cloud company and Tor exit.
Check a phone number against its country's numbering plan: format, country, line type
and original carrier.

## Authentication
Send your API key as a bearer token: `Authorization: Bearer vld_live_…`. Create keys
in the dashboard.

## Credits
One balance pays for every endpoint. `POST /v1/email/validate` costs 1 credit;
`POST /v1/email/validate/batch` costs 1 credit per address (up to 100);
`POST /v1/email/verify` costs 5 credits, or 1 when the result is `unknown` or the
address is invalid before the mailbox check; `POST /v1/domain/sender-readiness` costs
2 credits; `POST /v1/ip/lookup` costs 1 credit, and `POST /v1/ip/lookup/batch` 1 credit
per address (up to 100); `POST /v1/phone/validate` costs 1 credit, and
`POST /v1/phone/validate/batch` 1 credit per number (up to 100). A bulk job
(`/v1/bulk`) reserves the most it can cost when it starts and gives the unused credits
back when it ends. Every paid response
carries the remaining balance in `X-Credits-Remaining`.

## Rate limits
Responses carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`.
A `429` response includes `Retry-After`.

## Retries
Send an `Idempotency-Key` header (1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, for example a
UUID) with any paid `POST` (except the bulk routes) to retry it safely. A retry with the same key and body
within 24 hours is not charged again: the check runs again and the answer carries
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`, the first call's `credits_charged`, and your current
balance. A retry of `POST /v1/email/verify` returns the same mailbox check instead of
starting another, with that check's current credits (1 after an `unknown` refund). A
key can be retried 10 times. The same key with another body answers `422 idempotency_key_reused`;
while the first call still runs, `409 idempotency_key_in_use`. Responses are not
stored: they contain the addresses and numbers you sent. The bulk routes do not take
an `Idempotency-Key`: repeating a start answers `409 job_state`, and repeating an upload
creates another job.

## Test keys
A test key (`vld_test_…`, created in the dashboard) is free and needs no credits. It
answers only the inputs below, with fixed answers in the live format,
`credits_charged` 0 and the header `Touchmark-Test-Mode: true`; any other input answers
`400 test_input_required`. Use it in your tests and CI.

- Email: `valid@example.com`, `invalid@example.com`, `disposable@example.com`,
  `role@example.com`, `unknown@example.com` and `typo@gmial.com`. For
  `POST /v1/email/verify` also `mailbox-missing@example.com` and
  `catch-all@example.com`; test mailbox checks are answered at once.
- Sending domains: `ready.example.com` and `not-ready.example.com`.
- IP addresses: `192.0.2.1`, `198.51.100.1` (hosting), `203.0.113.1` (Tor exit) and
  `2001:db8::1`.
- Phone numbers: `+12015550123` and `+16135550199` (valid), `+447700900123` and
  `+15550000000` (invalid).

A batch with one non-test item is refused whole. `GET /v1/email/verify/{id}` answers 404
to a test key, as test verifications are never stored. `X-Credits-Remaining` shows the
real balance.

## Results and reasons
Every validation has one `result`. When several apply, the first in this list wins
(`invalid` > `unknown` > `risky` > `valid`):

- `invalid`: the address cannot receive mail. Its syntax is rejected, or its domain
  does not exist, publishes a null MX or has no mail records.
- `unknown`: DNS gave no definite answer (server failure, refusal or timeout). Try
  again later.
- `risky`: the domain accepts mail but belongs to a disposable-email provider.
- `valid`: the domain accepts mail and no risk flags apply.

`valid` from `validate` means the domain accepts mail and no risk flags apply. It does
**not** mean the mailbox exists: `validate` never contacts the mail server, so
`checks.mailbox.status` is `not_checked`.

`reasons` lists every rule that matched:

- `invalid_syntax`: the address fails the syntax policy. Quoted local parts, IP
  literals and single-label domains are rejected even where the RFCs allow them.
- `domain_not_found`: the domain does not exist (NXDOMAIN).
- `null_mx`: the domain publishes a null MX record (RFC 7505), so it accepts no mail.
- `no_mail_records`: the domain has neither an MX record nor an A or AAAA record.
- `dns_error`: the DNS lookup failed (server failure, refusal or timeout). The result
  is `unknown`, never `invalid`.
- `implicit_mx`: the domain has no MX record, so mail goes to its A or AAAA record.
  The domain still accepts mail.
- `disposable`: the domain, or a parent domain, belongs to a disposable-email
  provider. The result is `risky`.
- `free_provider`: the domain is a free email provider such as gmail.com. It does not
  change the result.
- `role_account`: the local part names a role, such as `info` or `support`, rather
  than a person (a `+tag` is ignored). It does not change the result.

Changes within `/v1` are additive: new fields and new reason codes may appear.
Clients must ignore unknown fields and unknown reason codes.

`datasets` gives the version of each domain list (`disposable`, `free_provider`) that
produced the flags. The values are opaque version identifiers: compare them for
equality, but do not parse them.

## Mailbox verification
`POST /v1/email/verify` runs the `validate` checks and then asks the address's mail
server whether the mailbox exists. It needs the `email:verify` scope and a completed
purchase (`403 tier_required` otherwise), and an account may submit 10 per second.
The mail server is never sent a message.

When the answer is known at once (the address is invalid, the mailbox was checked
recently, or the check cannot run) the call returns `200` with `status: "done"` and
`id: null`. Otherwise it returns `202` with an `id`, `status: "queued"`, the `validate`
result and `checks.mailbox.status` `pending`; 5 credits are charged, and 4 come back if
the check ends `unknown`. `GET /v1/email/verify/{id}` returns the check for free; with
`?wait=N` (up to 10) it waits that many seconds for the check to finish. A server that
asks to try again later is retried after 10 and 30 minutes. Results are kept for 7
days; once the check is done, `email`, `normalized` and `did_you_mean` are null, because
the address itself is not kept.

`checks.mailbox.status` is `exists`, `not_exists`, `catch_all` (the domain accepts mail
for any address), `unknown`, `pending`, or `not_checked` (the `validate` checks already
decided: the address is invalid, or DNS gave no answer). `not_exists` makes the result
`invalid` and adds the reason `mailbox_not_found`; `catch_all` makes it `risky` and adds
`catch_all`. An `unknown` mailbox makes the result `unknown`, and its reason appears in
`checks.mailbox.reason` and in `reasons`:

- `greylisted`: the server kept asking us to try again later.
- `connection_failed`: no mail server of the domain could be reached.
- `no_ipv4_server`: the domain's mail servers have no public IPv4 address, and mailbox
  checks use IPv4 only.
- `probe_blocked`: the server refused the check itself.
- `provider_unverifiable`: the provider accepts every address (Microsoft 365), or the
  server cannot take this address, so no answer would be meaningful; or its mail server
  offered TLS and then failed it, and we do not fall back to plaintext.
- `capacity_exceeded`: today's mailbox-check capacity is used up.
- `domain_limit`: this account checked 200 addresses at this domain today.
- `account_limit`: this account reached the daily limit of mailbox checks set in the
  dashboard's Settings.
- `smtp_unavailable`: mailbox checks are paused on our side.

## Sender readiness
`POST /v1/domain/sender-readiness` checks the DNS side of the bulk-sender rules: SPF
(one record, at most 10 DNS lookups, not `+all`), DKIM (a key under a common selector
or one you pass in `dkim_selectors`) and DMARC (`p` of `none`, `quarantine` or
`reject`). It also reports MX, MTA-STS, TLS-RPT and BIMI records. `dns_ready` gives
`pass`, `warn` or `fail` for Gmail, Yahoo and Microsoft, and `gaps` says what to fix.
DNS cannot show complaint rates, one-click unsubscribe or DMARC alignment in practice,
so `not_checked` lists them. When DNS lookups fail, the call returns
`503 upstream_unavailable` and costs nothing. After 10 such answers in 10 minutes an
account gets `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After`.

## IP lookup
`POST /v1/ip/lookup` takes one IPv4 or IPv6 address; `POST /v1/ip/lookup/batch` takes
up to 100 and answers in input order. They need the `ip:lookup` scope. A value that is
not an address is `422 validation_error` for the whole call, and nothing is charged.
Every answer comes from datasets held on our servers; the address is not sent anywhere.

- `country` and `continent` are a geolocation estimate at country level, from
  [IP Geolocation by DB-IP](https://db-ip.com). If you display them, keep that credit
  next to them.
- `asn` is the autonomous system that announces the address (DB-IP).
- `network` is `{"type": "hosting", "provider": …}` when the address belongs to the
  autonomous system of a hosting or cloud company (for example `aws`, `gcp`, `ovh`,
  `hetzner`), from our own list; `null` means it is not on that list, not that the
  address is residential.
- `tor_exit` says whether the address is a Tor exit (Tor Project list). It is `null`
  for IPv6: the list holds IPv4 exits only.
- `scope` is `global` for a public address. Private, shared (CGNAT), loopback,
  link-local, multicast, unspecified and reserved addresses get their scope and no
  other data, and still cost 1 credit.
- `datasets` gives the version of each dataset read, or `null` for one not loaded yet.

## Phone validation
`POST /v1/phone/validate` takes one phone number; `POST /v1/phone/validate/batch` takes
up to 100 and answers in input order. They need the `phone:validate` scope. Write
numbers in international form (`+44 20 7946 0000`), or pass `country` (an ISO 3166-1
alpha-2 code) for numbers written without `+`. Any string is answered and costs 1
credit; a malformed request (an empty `phone`, a number longer than 64 characters, an unknown `country`)
is `422 validation_error`, and nothing is charged. Every answer comes from Google's
libphonenumber numbering-plan data held on our servers; the number is not sent anywhere.

- `valid` means the number fits its country's numbering plan. It does not mean the
  number is assigned, in service or reachable. `reason` says why a number is not
  valid: `not_a_number`, `no_country_code` (written without `+` and no `country`
  given), `invalid_country_code`, `too_short`, `too_long`, `invalid_length` or
  `not_in_plan`.
- `type` is the line type from the numbering plan. The North American plan (the United
  States, Canada and much of the Caribbean) does not separate mobile numbers, so its
  numbers are `fixed_line_or_mobile`.
- `original_carrier` is the network the number range was first allocated to. Numbers
  move between networks, so it is not necessarily the current one. It is `null` for
  most landlines and North American numbers.
- `region` is the area of a landline range, such as a city. It describes the number
  range, not where anyone is.
- `country` is `null` for a number that is not valid and for non-geographic numbers
  (such as `+800`).
- `datasets` gives the version of the numbering-plan data used.

## Bulk jobs
For lists too long for a batch call, upload a CSV file (at most 20 MB) with
`POST /v1/bulk` as `multipart/form-data`: `file`, `kind` (`email`, `ip` or `phone`)
and, for phone numbers written without `+`, `country`. The answer is the job and its
pre-flight: rows, unique values and the most it can cost; nothing is charged yet.
`POST /v1/bulk/{id}/start` reserves that amount and queues the job (send
`{"email_column": n}` when the email column was not detected, and `{"smtp": true}`
to verify mailboxes, which needs the `email:verify` scope). Poll `GET /v1/bulk/{id}`
until `status` is `completed`, then download `GET /v1/bulk/{id}/result`. Unused credits
come back when the job ends. Each call needs the scope of the job's kind. A job in
the wrong state for a call answers `409 job_state`. The dashboard lists the same jobs.
Test keys cannot run bulk jobs.

### Webhooks
Start a job with `{"webhook_url": "https://…"}` (an `https` URL whose host is a name,
not an IP address, and resolves to public addresses) and Touchmark POSTs an event to it when the job ends:
`{"id": …, "type": "bulk_job.completed", "created_at": …, "data": <the job>}`, with
`bulk_job.failed` and `bulk_job.cancelled` for the other endings. Answer with any
`2xx` within 10 seconds. A failed delivery is retried, with the same body and
`Touchmark-Event-Id`, 1, 5 and 15 minutes and 1, 3, 6 and 12 hours after the job
ended; the job's `webhook` part shows the attempts and the last error. Redirects are
not followed.

Each event carries `Touchmark-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`. Check it with
your signing secret (Settings → Webhooks in the dashboard): compute HMAC-SHA256 with
the whole `whsec_…` string, as UTF-8 bytes, as the key over
`<t>.<raw body>`, compare it with `v1` (lowercase hex) in constant time,
and refuse events whose `t` is more than 5 minutes old.

## Errors
Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` documents with a stable `code`.
See the [error reference](/docs/errors).

## MCP server
AI agents can call these checks as tools through the MCP server at `https://api.touchmark.dev/mcp`
(Streamable HTTP). Send your API key as for any other call:
`Authorization: Bearer vld_live_…`. Each tool calls the endpoint above it stands
for and costs the same credits, with the same scopes and limits: `validate_email`
(1), `verify_email` (up to 5; waits up to about 25 seconds, then returns the
check's `id`), `get_email_verification` (free), `check_sender_readiness` (2),
`lookup_ip` (1), `validate_phone` (1) and `get_account` (free).

Claude Code:
`claude mcp add --transport http touchmark https://api.touchmark.dev/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer vld_live_…"`

Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`):
`{"mcpServers": {"touchmark": {"url": "https://api.touchmark.dev/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer vld_live_…"}}}}`

VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`):
`{"servers": {"touchmark": {"type": "http", "url": "https://api.touchmark.dev/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer vld_live_…"}}}}`

claude.ai and ChatGPT: add a custom connector with the URL `https://api.touchmark.dev/mcp`, then sign in to
Touchmark and allow it. The connector gets its own API key ("<client> (MCP
connector)"); revoke that key on the API keys page to disconnect it.

## SDKs
Official client libraries for TypeScript, Python and Go, under the MIT licence:
[github.com/icomi-software/touchmark-sdks](https://github.com/icomi-software/touchmark-sdks).

- TypeScript: `npm install touchmark`, then
  `const tm = new Touchmark({ apiKey: process.env.TOUCHMARK_API_KEY })` and
  `await tm.email.validate({ email: "jane@acme.com" })`.
- Python: `pip install touchmark`, then `tm = Touchmark()` (reads
  `TOUCHMARK_API_KEY`) and `tm.email.validate(email="jane@acme.com")`.
- Go: `go get github.com/icomi-software/touchmark-sdks/go`, then
  `tm, err := touchmark.New(touchmark.Options{})` (reads `TOUCHMARK_API_KEY`) and
  `tm.Email.Validate(ctx, touchmark.ValidateRequest{Email: "jane@acme.com"})`.

Each charged call sends an `Idempotency-Key`, so the SDKs retry network errors and
`5xx` answers without charging twice.

## Terms
Use of the API is subject to the [Terms of Service](https://touchmark.dev/legal/terms)
and the [Acceptable Use Policy](https://touchmark.dev/legal/acceptable-use).

## Status
Current availability and past incidents: <https://status.touchmark.dev/>.
